note: Miller->Volcker; Oct-1979 'Volcker shock' shift to reserve targeting. Monthly eff. peaked ~17.6% Apr-1980 (daily/target briefly ~20%). Brief sharp NBER recession 1980-01 to 1980-07; Carter credit controls.
Double-dip: after mid-1980 easing to ~9%, re-hiked to ~19-20% by Jun-1981 to break inflation. NBER recession 1981-07 to 1982-11, unemployment >10%. Classic hard landing; inflation broken.
Volcker post-disinflation tightening 8.5%->11.5%. NO recession followed; one of only two 1980s+ episodes with no yield-curve inversion (St. Louis Fed). Early soft landing.
Greenspan tightening in 18 steps, +331bp (St. Louis Fed). Post-1987-crash re-tightening vs inflation creep. NBER recession 1990-07 to 1991-03 (Gulf War oil spike compounded).
THE classic soft landing (Greenspan): pre-emptive doubling 3%->6% in 7 moves, incl. 75bp Nov-1994. Expansion continued to 2001. The canonical benchmark case.
Late-cycle tightening into dot-com bubble; capped with 50bp May-2000. NBER recession 2001-03 to 2001-11 (dot-com bust; 9/11 compounded).
17 consecutive 25bp 'measured pace' hikes 1%->5.25%. Yield curve inverted 2006. NBER recession 2007-12 to 2009-06 = Global Financial Crisis (housing/credit).

Slow ZIRP-exit lift-off, target 0-0.25%->2.25-2.50%. NBER recession began 2020-02 but cause was COVID-19 pandemic (exogenous shock), NOT the tightening. Flag: timing-only, not a policy-induced hard landing.
Fastest cycle in 4 decades vs post-COVID inflation; target 0-0.25%->5.25-5.50%, +525bp. No recession as of mid-2026 -> judged a soft landing so far / 'immaculate disinflation'; status provisional.
